title: Going Beyond Word Matching Syntax Improves In-context Example Selection for Machine Translation

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 7 and Table 12 at the end of the paper
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The document labels a table as "Table 7: Size of WikiMatrix before and after pre-processing and the percentage of reserved sentences after pre-processing for 6 languages," but the immediately following table instead has columns "Strategy" and "Output" and contains FR-EN model translations. That content is then labeled "Table 12: Outputs of FR-EN translation under different selection strategies." Thus Table 7's claimed dataset-size statistics are absent, while the same displayed table is assigned incompatible Table 7 and Table 12 identities.

The paper states, "An example of our prompt is shown in Figure 1." The supplied Figure 1 is only 43 by 32 pixels and contains no legible prompt, demonstrations, language-pair instruction, or generation template. It cannot serve as the claimed prompt example or permit inspection/reproduction of the prompt format.

The full paper contains an uncaptioned Figure 0 before Figure 1 and an uncaptioned Figure 4 after Figure 3, but neither is introduced or discussed anywhere in the text. Conversely, the paper's figure references concern Figures 1--3. These unexplained inserted figures and the numbering mismatch make the figure record internally corrupted and require correction.

The central claim is repeated several times: the methods obtain the highest COMET score on "11 out of 12 translation directions." The paper says the evidence is in Table 1 and additionally invokes Tables 2, 4, and 8--11, but those result tables are not present in the supplied full text. No per-direction COMET values, rankings, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests are supplied from which the 11/12 claim can be checked. The conclusion therefore presents a numerical comparative result as established without the reported evidence.

The text explicitly relies on numerous tables that are absent: Table 1 is said to contain all 12-direction results; Table 2 the CTQScorer comparison; Table 3 the example-selection comparison; Table 4 computation times; Table 5 licenses; Table 6 parser models; Tables 8--11 BLEU and COMET results. Apart from the mislabeled Table 7/Table 12 content, none of these tables is included. This omits essential experimental results, resource disclosures, and appendix material that the paper claims to provide.

The paper asserts that "All the experiments are completely reproducible since our selection methods are deterministic and sampling is disabled during LLM generation." Determinism and disabled sampling do not establish complete reproducibility: exact prompts, generation settings, model/checkpoint and software versions, spaCy model versions, preprocessing implementation, retrieval-index construction, data snapshots, and the missing result/configuration tables are also required. The statement materially overclaims what follows from the stated reasons.
